rubric.judge: Direct review by the Codex assistant; no judge model or metric LLM.
rubric.ragas.context_precision: RAGAS-style average precision evaluated separately for each retrieval-query leg, then averaged across legs. Reset rank at each query and de-duplicate identical filename/text chunks within that leg, so a corrective leg is not treated as if it were appended below the initial ranking. The hand-labeled expected_source documents define relevance. Use 0 for a leg with no expected-source context.
rubric.ragas.context_recall: Fraction of hand-labeled expected_source documents represented anywhere in the retrieval trace.
rubric.ragas.faithfulness: Fraction of factual claims in the actual answer supported by the retrieval trace. Use 1 for an answer containing no unsupported factual claims and 0 for a wrong abstention on an answerable case.
rubric.deepeval.answer_correctness: Fraction of required expected-answer facts stated correctly, with unsupported or contradictory additions reducing the score.
rubric.deepeval.hallucination_rate: Fraction of actual-answer factual claims that are unsupported by or contradict the retrieved evidence. Lower is better.
rubric.deepeval.citation_accuracy: Fraction of factual claims whose adjacent filename citations point to passages that support those claims. Missing required citations score 0.
rubric.custom.abstention_accuracy: Binary: 1 when an unanswerable case abstains, or an adversarial case refuses, corrects the false premise, or flags and ignores an injection as expected; else 0.

trials.question: What does FR-006 require?
trials.expected_answer: A retrieval-only endpoint for debugging the top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens.
trials.answer: Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation. FR-008: The system shall keep API keys, uploaded documents, and generated indexes out of Git. [01_product_requirements.docx]

retrieval_trace.text: Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx Agentic CRAG RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Expected answer: /opt/agentic-crag/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Question D: Which risk has the highest probability score? Expected source: risk workbook. Expected answer: R-004, missing source citations, probability 0.70. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. Pass Criteria For a recruiter demo, the system should achieve at least 80 percent answer correctness on the curated test questions. For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time.

Non-Functional Requirements NFR-001: The demo must run on a low-cost EC2 instance for portfolio evaluation, with the understanding that indexing may be slower on very small machines. NFR-002: The browser interface should remain simple enough for a non-technical evaluator to upload documents and ask questions without setup instructions inside the app. NFR-003: The backend should expose explicit health checks so deployment problems can be diagnosed through curl before testing the UI. NFR-004: The repository should be small, clean, and free of generated local artifacts. NFR-005: The application should make retrieval evidence visible to reduce hallucination risk and improve trust. Known Scope Boundaries The current release does not include authentication. Public demo deployments should only be used temporarily or behind a controlled network. The current release does not include reranking. Retrieval uses vector similarity and a small top-k value suitable for a lightweight demo. The current release does not include hybrid BM25 plus vector search. Exact identifier queries may be improved in a future version. The current release does not process scanned PDFs with OCR. Text must be extractable from the uploaded files. The current release does not store collections in S3 or a managed vector database. Local disk is used for simplicity and cost control. Acceptance Criteria A reviewer can upload the full demo corpus and ask: What is FR-006? The answer should mention the retrieval-only endpoint and cite this product requirements document. A reviewer can ask whether authentication is included. The answer should state that authentication is not included in the current release. A reviewer can ask what success target is defined for fact-seeking questions. The answer should report the 85 percent target. A reviewer can ask whether scanned PDFs are supported. The answer should say OCR is not included and text must be extractable.

Document filename: 01_product_requirements.docx Agentic CRAG Product Requirements Document Version 2.4 - Demo Corpus Executive Summary Agentic CRAG is a document assistant for retrieval augmented generation over uploaded business documents. The product goal is to let a user upload project material, create a searchable collection, and ask grounded questions with visible source evidence. The demo release is designed for small to medium public documents. It is not intended for confidential legal, medical, financial, or customer records because the final language model answer may be generated by an external model provider. The product success target for the demo is to answer at least 85 percent of fact-seeking test questions correctly when the answer exists in the uploaded documents, while refusing unsupported questions when the answer is absent. Personas The primary persona is an early-career analyst who has several PDFs, Word files, and spreadsheets and wants quick answers without reading every page manually. The secondary persona is a recruiter or technical reviewer evaluating whether the project demonstrates practical RAG engineering, deployment awareness, and clear explanation of tradeoffs. The tertiary persona is a project manager who wants comparison summaries across release notes, budgets, risk logs, and deployment documents. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation.
